key_insight: A broader multimorbidity pattern—captured as 16 shared functional units across diagnoses—was linked to steeper age-related disease incidence and to distinct genetic architecture.
clinical_relevance: This work may help researchers prioritize disease networks and genetic targets relevant to chronic disease progression, but it does not itself establish a treatment or clinical decision rule.
method: Analyzed UK Biobank linked health records across 232 diagnoses in 502,355 participants.
Used generative representation learning to derive 16 functional units from pre-assessment co-occurrence patterns.
Compared each diagnosis’s linked functional-unit breadth with later incidence and tested genetic signals in external cohorts and fine-mapping analyses.
evidence_signal: The main association was strong and consistent: diagnoses linked to more functional units showed steeper age dependence of incidence (Spearman rho = 0.50; 0.46 for 196 diagnoses with rising hazards).
watch_item: The findings are observational and cohort-based, so they support association rather than causation and may not translate directly to individual patient care.
paper_title: Functional organization of multimorbidity links chronic disease incidence to shared genetic architecture
